a.xlink:title: This section asks only whether the platform must provide RWX at all, and answers it from `/shared` because that is the one place the requirement is forced. It is not the only candidate consumer and may not end up the largest. Home volumes are the bigger question — RWX there is not required by any contract, but it is the move that would dissolve the per-user node pin and the cross-AZ constraint at once, which is why it gets its own topic. Cross-pack sharing is a third, where no requirement is established yet and object storage may serve it instead. So: `/shared` settles whether, and the topics below settle how much.

a.xlink:title: RWX is unnecessary if every collaborating pod is permanently constrained to one node.
Permanent single-node co-location of collaborating pods is not an acceptable production platform constraint.
RWO could replace RWX if every pod sharing a group directory were constrained to one node.

a.xlink:title: Nebari has no AWS identity per Keycloak user and no secrets-management system — one IAM identity deploys the cluster, and JupyterLab pods carry no AWS credentials (Marcelo Villa, 2026-08-13). Group-scoped access would mean mapping Keycloak groups onto IAM policy or bucket prefixes, which Marcelo called a mess that arrives quickly. Mounting a bucket as a filesystem (goofys-style) makes the paths look normal but moves none of this.

a.xlink:title: Object storage is complementary storage, not a transparent replacement for the DSP shared directory.
Object storage complements the shared filesystem but cannot satisfy the shared-directory contract on its own.
a.text: Object storage does not remove RWX

a.xlink:title: S3-compatible object storage could replace the shared filesystem.

A data catalog — Kim Pevey named an open-source Databricks Unity Catalog equivalent on 2026-08-13 — could own dataset entitlements above object storage, so access control stops being IAM plumbing and workloads resolve what they may read through the catalog API. Proposed, not evaluated; the program is already prototyping on Databricks.

a.xlink:title: Reach for object storage rather than RWX in any scenario it can serve, and treat a shared filesystem as the fallback for what genuinely needs POSIX. Stated as a working preference (James Olds, 2026-08-14), not a team decision, and it cuts hardest at cross-pack sharing, where no RWX requirement has been established at all. Its own costs are unsettled and named in Object storage changes the product contract: no per-user AWS identity to key access on, unproven small-file and metadata performance, and no in-cluster option short of running MinIO or equivalent — which trades the managed service for another storage system to operate.
